topics.topic: How canonical_bytes handles lone surrogates before the UTF-8 depth check
questions: Which requirement must change: calling json_depth first on UTF-8 bytes, or accepting that a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 encoding and must be rejected before those bytes can be produced?

A Python string containing a lone surrogate cannot be encoded as UTF-8 with the standard strict encoding, so the required initial UTF-8 conversion raises UnicodeEncodeError before canonical_bytes can raise NonCanonicalValueError for the surrogate; which requirement must change, or what encoding/error handling reconciles them?

A Python str containing a lone surrogate cannot be encoded as UTF-8 normally, so the required pre-parse depth check raises UnicodeEncodeError before canonical_bytes can raise NonCanonicalValueError for the lone surrogate; which requirement must change, or what specified encoding/error handling reconciles them?

quotes: otherwise MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
judgement.why: The required observable result for a lone surrogate is explicitly NonCanonicalValueError; the internal method used to obtain bytes for the preceding depth scan is not prescribed.

topics.topic: How json_depth detects a closing quote after an even-length backslash run
questions: How are these reconciled when a closing quote is preceded by an even-length run of backslashes, so the immediately preceding backslash is itself escaped and the quote ends the string?

quotes: a string running from a double quote to the next double quote not escaped by a backslash
judgement.why: A quote after an even-length backslash run is not escaped because the immediately preceding backslash is itself escaped, so the quoted rule identifies it as the closing quote.
